metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% in such regimes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2 days above true peak, then apply mean reversion toward 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., +0.7+ after -0.5+), model delays correction; adjust forecast downward by 3–5% for next 3–5 days to avoid overconfidence.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral; apply 2–5% downward bias if sentiment is < 0.2.
- When true outcome shows sudden drop (e.g., >15% fall from prior day), model often fails to recognize it; add 1–3 day lag correction: forecast should be 1–2 days below true drop point.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model tends to ignore the trend; apply 10–15% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
